title: Property-Charge Shortfall at Short-Sale Closing
content:
# Property-charge shortfall at a short-sale closing — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction

On the payoff case of an Approved Short Sale Payoff requested by the borrower of record, the property-charge shortfall is one of the amounts paid from the price at closing. It is figured from the set-aside, held under the Set-Aside Accounts product, that pays the loan's property charges, and from its bills.

**Fully Funded LESA (Mandatory or Borrower-Elected).** Its shortfall source bills the borrower for what the set-aside cannot pay. The shortfall is the sum of that set-aside's approval bills less its set-aside balance, not below 0.00. An approval bill is, for each of property tax bill, hazard insurance bill and flood insurance bill, the received bill of that type on the Fully Funded LESA with the latest due date, when its payment date (its due date less the plan's tax payment lead days for a tax bill, and less its insurance payment lead days for a hazard or flood bill) falls no later than 30 calendar days after the approval date. Where several such bills of one type share that latest due date, their billed amounts are taken together.

**Partially Funded LESA.** A Partially Funded LESA pays no bill. The shortfall is the sum, over the three bill types, of the bills that set-aside declined of each type with the latest due date, counted when that due date falls no later than 30 calendar days after the approval date; several declined bills of one type due on that latest due date are taken together. The test here is the due date itself, with no lead days.

**Other set-asides.** A loan with an active Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve, or with no such set-aside, has no shortfall (0.00).

## Hypothetical cases

| Set-aside | Bills | Shortfall |
|---|---|---|
| Fully Funded LESA, balance USD 1200.00 | approval bills of USD 1500.00 (tax) and USD 400.00 (hazard) | USD 700.00 |
| Fully Funded LESA, balance USD 3000.00 | approval bills totalling USD 1900.00 | 0.00 |
| Partially Funded LESA | latest declined tax bill USD 2100.00 due 20 days after the approval date; latest declined flood bill due 45 days after | USD 2100.00 |
| Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve | any | 0.00 |

The 30 days are the plan's good-through period. All amounts and dates are invented.
